newsitem.title: USA: Epitope sues to rescind A&W acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Epitope sues to rescind A&W acquisition.

text.p: Epitope Inc. has filed a $20 million lawsuit against the former owners of Andrew & Williamson Sales Co. and is seeking to rescind its acquisition of the food packaging firm, which distributed strawberries linked to a hepatitis outbreak.

In a statement Monday, Epitope said it is alleging fraud and breach of contract in connection with Andrew & Williamson's distribution of frozen strawberries through the Agriculture Department's school lunch program.
The frozen strawberries sold have been associated with an outbreak of hepatitis A among school children and teachers in several Michigan schools last week.

Epitope said the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention associated the outbreak with strawberries that were grown in Mexico and processed at the Andrew & Williamson plant in San Diego on three days last year -- April 19, May 7 and May 8.

Andrew & Williamson's former chief executive had certified on Nov. 27, that the berries were grown in the United States, Epitope said. The biotechnology company acquired Andrew & Williamson on Dec. 12.
Andrew & Williamson Chief Executive Fred Williamson resigned April 2, after a massive recall of the berries was announced.
Epitope said Monday it is cooperating fully with federal and state regulatory agencies investigating the matter.

In the suit, filed in the United States District Court for the District of Oregon, Epitope seeks $20 million in actual and punitive damages and rescission of its purchase of Andrew & Williamson stock.

Epitope charges the former owners of Andrew & Williamson defrauded Epitope in connection with the sale, violated federal and state securities laws and breached contractual warranties and representations by failing to disclose the false certification of the origin of the strawberries.

It also charges Andrew & Williamson committed fraud by certifying it was not subject to liability for any past or continuing violation of any law, and by saying it knew of no conditions or liabilities that might have a material adverse effect on Andrew & Williamson's business or financial condition.
Shares of Epitope rose $1.50 to $9.375 on the American Stock Exchange.
